subject.title: fix: strip volatile output from exec result hash to fix no-progress detection (#93917)

question: Should loop detection treat every same-command nonzero exit as identical across intervening tool calls, or preserve semantic output/intervening progress before accumulating the blocking streak?
rationale: Both choices affect core agent availability: the broad fingerprint stops the reported runaway loop, but it can also terminate legitimate iterative test, build, SSH, or diagnostic workflows whose command and exit code remain unchanged while the underlying result improves.

options.title: Narrow the fingerprint
options.body: Preserve a normalized semantic output signature or reset the streak across state-changing calls so only genuinely unchanged nonzero retries accumulate.

options.title: Accept broad blocking
options.body: Merge the output-insensitive policy only with explicit owner acceptance and regression proof documenting that repeated same-command nonzero outcomes may block despite changed diagnostics.

options.title: Pause pending policy
options.body: Keep the PR open until an agent-runtime owner defines which intervening actions and output changes count as progress.

recommendation.title: Narrow the fingerprint
recommendation.body: Preserve a normalized semantic output signature or reset the streak across state-changing calls so only genuinely unchanged nonzero retries accumulate.

likelyOwner.reason: They already reviewed the foreground exec contract and the contributor explicitly requested their decision on the remaining output policy.
